title: ZERO44 brings carbon insetting and regulatory compliance together in industry-first solution
summary: ZERO44's new Carbon Insetting module aims to streamline how operators allocate low-carbon fuel credits, separating those used for FuelEU Maritime compliance from voluntary emission reduction sales. This software primarily optimizes financial returns on already-purchased alternative fuels, meticulously managing "additionality" to prevent double-counting reductions for both regulatory targets and cargo owners' Scope 3 claims. While offering financial flexibility for a select few, this tool primarily refines emissions accounting and does not inherently pressure the vast majority of the fleet still burning high-carbon fuels or struggling with excessive carbon intensity.
content:
ZERO44, the maritime emissions compliance platform, has launched its new Carbon Insetting module, the industry’s first software to bring regulatory compliance and carbon insetting decision-making into a single solution.

Carbon insetting lets operators sell the emission reductions from low-carbon fuel use directly to cargo owners who want to cut their own Scope 3 emissions. It is already common in the container and bulk segments. For operators, it is the only way to recover part of a low-carbon fuel investment from the specific customer who benefits from it, something FuelEU Maritime cannot do.

The catch is additionality: reductions sold on the voluntary market must not also count toward FuelEU targets. Until now, operators have tracked this manually, using spreadsheets to keep volumes reserved for insetting separate from volumes used for compliance, across a fleet where prices and compliance balances change daily.

ZERO44’s Carbon Insetting module removes that manual work. Built on the same Bunker Delivery Note and Proof of Sustainability data operators already use for compliance reporting, it shows the value of every fuel volume as FuelEU surplus compared with an insetting certificate, using live surplus and inset prices.

Once an operator allocates a volume to insetting, ZERO44 automatically deducts it from the vessel’s FuelEU compliance balance, so the surplus to be released rather than banked is always correct at reporting time. The underlying data can be pushed straight to the operator’s registry of choice, removing duplicate entry between systems.

Friederike Hesse, Co-Founder and Managing Director at ZERO44, says: “Every tonne of low-carbon fuel an operator buys is money that can come back through FuelEU surplus or through insetting, but rarely both at the same value. Our customers can now see, for every bunkering event, which route pays more today and act on it. That turns a cost they were already carrying into revenue they were leaving on the table.”
